12.0.s.en: (1) Plucking the ears of corn on the Sabbath

12.0.0.en: "The Sabbath": the day of the Lord among the Jews, for God commanded that it be set apart for worship, but the elders of the Jews forbade even necessary works on it. The glory of Sunday surpassed the glory of the Sabbath, because on it the Lord of glory rose, so it is considered the Lord's Day in the New Testament.

12.0.1.en: "Through the corn": Christ wanted to be alone with His disciples, so He went with them to the fields.

12.0.2.en: "Plucked the ears of corn": the hungry were permitted to pluck some ears and rub them in their hands and eat them to satisfy their hunger. It is understood from this that the disciples were poor and needed necessary food, since they had no food.

12.0.3.en: "That which is not lawful to do": they forbade some works on the Sabbath, among them the plucking of ears of corn. The Law did not state this, but it was among the mistaken excessive interpretations that they added, and it conflicts with the necessary needs of man.

12.0.4.en: Christ was walking with His disciples on the Sabbath through the cornfields, continuing to teach them. After a while they became hungry, so they plucked some ears to eat, and this was permitted in the Law and is not considered stealing (Deut 23:25). But the Pharisees considered it a harvesting of wheat, and work is forbidden on the Sabbath day, so they objected to Christ, because He did not prevent His disciples from doing it.

12.0.5.en: Though work is forbidden on the Sabbath day so that they may be free for the worship of God, necessary works such as eating are not forbidden, so this was a vain accusation from the Pharisees, since they counted the disciples' satisfying their hunger as a harvesting of wheat, and this shows their ill intent and the narrowness of their interpretation of the concept of rest on the Sabbath day.

12.1.0.en: "The house of God": the Tabernacle of the congregation.

12.1.1.en: "The showbread": twelve loaves that were placed on a table in the Holy Place on the right, and none entered the Holy Place except the priests, so only the priests ate it, as a symbol of the special grace of the sacrament of the priesthood in the New Testament. Christ reminded the disciples of what David did on the Sabbath day, when he and those with him were hungry, for they entered and ate of the showbread, which it is not lawful to eat except for the priests, but out of necessity, and so that they would not faint from hunger, they ate of it.

12.1.2.en: And King David is very honored, and a point of reference for the Jews from whom to learn, so David's understanding of the spirit of the commandment, and not its letter, appears here; he did not intend to break the commandment, but the matter requires an understanding of the spirit of the commandment, that is, flexibility in carrying it out.

12.1.3.en: This is the first proof that the disciples did not err in plucking the ears of corn on the Sabbath day.

12.2.0.en: "The Law" (the Torah): the five books of Moses, and what is meant is specifically the book of Numbers, where it mentions the offering of sacrifices on the Sabbath day.

12.2.1.en: "Profane the Sabbath": that is, break the rest imposed on this day.

12.2.2.en: "And are blameless": because they obey the Law by offering the services required in the Law.

12.2.3.en: Christ gave a second proof, namely the works that the priests do on the Sabbath day in the Temple, for they do not intend to break the Sabbath, but these are works of service connected with the worship of God, that is, the offering of sacrifices. What is meant is abstaining from ordinary works and material gains, and devoting oneself to spiritual work, and being content only with the necessary needs of man.

12.3.0.en: If occupation with the Temple permits any work or service that it needs, then before us is Christ, the Lord of the Temple, who is greater than it; indeed the Jewish Temple signifies Him, for He is the One who will offer Himself as a sacrifice on the altar of the Cross. Therefore the disciples ate some ears of corn to satisfy their hunger, and to remain occupied with hearing His teachings and serving Him, and this is the highest purpose.

12.4.0.en: "The guiltless": the poor disciples who needed to satisfy their hunger, for they are guiltless of any fault.

12.4.1.en: Christ pointed to the words of God in Hosea the prophet (Hos 6:6), that He desires mercy and not sacrifice, that is, that what is meant is that the work of mercy is more important than literal adherence to sacrifice while the heart is empty of love and given to accusing and condemning others.

12.4.2.en: How did they not feel the hunger of the disciples, and their necessary need to eat?! It is hardness of heart on the part of the Pharisees, and so the righteousness of the disciples and the wickedness of the Pharisees appeared.

12.5.0.en: "Lord of the Sabbath": that is, the One who laid down the law of the Sabbath, and who alone may permit what He sees fit, and add what must be attended to, so He added the sanctification of Sunday, and it became the Lord's Day through His Resurrection on it. Christ affirms that He is the giver of the Law, which includes the sanctification of the Sabbath day, so He of course does not want to break the commandment, but its spirit must be understood and applied well. And this is a third proof in defense of the disciples for their plucking the ears of corn, since they have with them the Lord of the Sabbath, who is able to permit what He sees fit.

12.5.1.en: Do not judge by appearance and condemn others, but make excuses for them, and be merciful to sinners as God has compassion on you and has mercy on you.

12.6.s.en: (2) The healing of the man with the withered hand

12.6.0.en: "Accuse Him": bring a complaint in their local councils that He is a transgressor.

12.6.1.en: After He had passed through the fields, He went to one of the synagogues of the Jews as was His custom to teach there, and all the sick were following Him that He might heal them; and a man came whose hand was paralyzed, hoping that Christ would heal him. The Pharisees noticed that the man would ask Christ for healing, so they hastened to ask Him, not out of inquiry but with malice: Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath day? They considered that healing is one of the worldly works, being the work of a physician who treats the sick, and not a miracle and a mercy that Christ offers to the needy; and this shows their ill intent and their mistaken interpretation.

12.7.0.en: Christ answered their question with another question, namely: If someone has a sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath day, will he not hasten to rescue it and lift it out of the pit so that it does not die? This work is not permitted, but it is excepted as a work of mercy to rescue the sheep, so how much more is a sick man more important than a sheep? Consequently, healing is lawful as a work of mercy on the Sabbath day. Then Christ, by His divine authority, commanded the man with the withered hand to stretch it out, and he obeyed in faith, and it was healed immediately.

12.7.1.en: It is to be noted that Christ only commanded and did not touch him, and the man stretched out his hand, and stretching out the hand is not forbidden on the Sabbath. Thus He healed him, and did not violate even their narrow, mistaken teachings, so they found no charge against Him.

12.7.2.en: How great is the obedience of this sick man: although his hand was paralyzed, he believed the word of Christ, and when he tried to stretch it out it moved with him, and he was healed immediately.

12.7.3.en: May you obey the commandments of God however difficult they seem, and accept the teachings of the Church and the guidance of your father of confession, confident of the power of God that supports you, so that you find nothing impossible before you, because Satan makes you imagine your weakness and your inability to be freed from sin and acquire virtues, so do not believe him, and be sure that obedience brings you out of his authority and grants you all blessings.

12.8.0.en: "That they might destroy him": this is the first attempt to kill Him.

12.8.1.en: "Great multitudes": of Jews and Gentiles, as appears in (v. 21).

12.8.2.en: When the wickedness of the Pharisees appeared before the righteousness of Christ and His mercy to His disciples and to the sick, they were greatly enraged and tried to kill Him, and He did not resist them using the power of His divinity, but fled from their presence, because He was occupied with completing the preaching and healing the needy, and also to teach us not to resist evil with evil, but to flee from it, so He charged the crowds to hide Him among them, in order to continue His teaching and doing good for all the needy, and because He was humble and did not seek earthly glory.

12.9.0.en: Christ showed this in a manner that appeared weak, contrary to what the Jews expected of the awaited Messiah, that He would be strong, establish a kingdom for them and free them from the authority of the Romans. And this of course is a mistaken interpretation by the Jews that God did not intend, but what matters is that He free them from sin, and reign over their hearts, and not the earthly kingship they claim, and therefore St. Matthew cited the prophecy of Isaiah about Christ (Isa 42:1-4), which shows His meekness and His not resisting evil with evil.

12.10.0.en: "Whom I have chosen": Christ alone is the One chosen by God and able to redeem mankind, and no angel or man can do this work.

12.10.1.en: "In whom my soul is well pleased": as the Father declared from heaven at His Baptism in the Jordan, for He is the object of the Father's pleasure because He accomplishes our salvation.

12.10.2.en: "I will put my spirit upon him": a declaration that the Holy Spirit is in the Son, as He appeared in the form of a dove at His Baptism, but He is united with Him from eternity because He is His Spirit, so it is a declaration to us as human beings that we may believe that He is God. "The Gentiles": a clear proof that salvation is offered to the whole world.

12.10.3.en: The Father speaks about the Son saying that He puts His Spirit upon Him, and He is at the same time the Spirit of the Son, who is the Holy Spirit. Thus He declares the Holy Trinity, who appears in the Incarnation of Christ, who proclaims the truth to mankind with meekness and love, when He says: my servant and my beloved.

12.10.4.en: If you are united with Christ and become a member of His body, the Church, you will be beloved of God and He will be pleased with you.

12.11.0.en: Among the characteristics of the meek Christ is that He does not meet people's evil with another evil, so He does not quarrel with the wicked, and does not become angry with shouting that makes others stumble in the streets, because He is calm within with true meekness.

12.12.0.en: The love of Christ appears in His care for every person however weak or hopeless he may seem, like the reed that has been struck and was about to break, or the wick from which the fire has gone out and nothing remains but smoke rising from it.

12.12.1.en: For He supports the very weak person until he becomes strong and is filled with Him, and overcomes his sins and weaknesses, and has a place in heaven.

12.12.2.en: He supports the reed and kindles the wick and cares for it, until He completes His work of showing forth the truth in all hearts, so that they overcome sin and are freed from it.

12.13.0.en: By this love He gives hope to the whole world. For if the Jews reject the Gentiles because of their distance from God, Christ preaches to them and seeks their salvation however weak they are, so that they leave the worship of idols and return to Him.

12.13.1.en: It is a great hope offered to you, however much your sins dominate you, or your problems seem to have no solution, for Christ loves you, and He is able to save you from your troubles. Trust in Him, and arise, begin anew with Him.

12.14.0.en: Satan entered a man, and made him lose his mind, his sight and his speech. They brought him to Christ and He healed him, that is, He cast Satan out of him, so he returned sane, seeing and speaking.

12.14.1.en: Sin makes you lose your sound thinking, so you do not see God and do not speak His commandments. So hasten to repentance, that you may regain your humanity in Christ.

12.15.0.en: "Amazed": he wondered and was greatly astonished.

12.15.1.en: "Son of David": as God promised that Christ would come from the seed of David.

12.15.2.en: "Beelzebub": see the commentary on (ch. 10:24-25), and accusing Christ of a relationship with him is a kind of contempt for Him, and means that His power is from the devils and not from God.

12.15.3.en: When the Jews saw the power of the miracle, they said that He is the awaited Messiah, the Son of David. But the Pharisees, because of their pride and love of worldly positions, found Christ to be a rival to them, since He had become a spiritual leader of the Jews, and by this they would lose their standing, so they hastened to oppose the miracle by accusing Christ that, by a special agreement between Him and Beelzebub the prince of the devils, He made this demon come out, and the man returned healthy; that is, they accused Christ of sorcery and of dealing with demons, in order to turn people away from following Him and from being amazed at His divine authority.

12.16.0.en: "Jesus knew their thoughts": this shows His divinity and His knowledge of the unseen, and of what is inside people without hearing them.

12.16.1.en: Christ gave the Pharisees a logical argument for the falsity of their accusation, so that the Jews would not doubt but stand firm in their faith in Him and in following Him, namely that if division occurs in any kingdom it is laid waste, since each party opposes the other. So if this happened in the kingdom of Satan, it would mean that the prince of the devils sets free those of mankind who follow him, and this is against his plan, because he wants to harm human beings and turn them away from God. So Satan cannot work against himself, or his kingdom would be laid waste, and this is illogical. Consequently, the casting out of this demon is by the power of God, and not by an agreement with the prince of the devils.

12.17.0.en: Then He gave a second logical argument, namely His disciples, that is, the sons of the Jewish nation who cast out demons. It is known among the Jews that the disciples were simple and had no experience in dealing with demons, sorcery and divination. So the disciples' casting out of demons judges the Pharisees' accusation to be false, just as the Jews do not object to any of their own who cast out demons, such as the seven sons of Sceva (Acts 19:14), even if this was a mere claim and not a real ability. Why then do they object to Christ and accuse Him of sorcery, except that they envy Him, and try to cast doubt on His divine power?

12.18.0.en: Satan came out by the power of the Spirit of God, and not by sorcery, and this means that He is the awaited Messiah. "The kingdom of God is come unto you": that is, Christ has come to reign over hearts, so why do you oppose Him with your evil thoughts?

12.19.0.en: And Christ gave a third proof that He casts out Satan by the authority of His divinity, which is that it is not possible to seize the possessions of a strong person unless we are able to bind him first. Consequently, it is not possible to cast a demon out of a person unless we have authority over the demons to bind them, and so command them to come out. That is, Christ is stronger than the demons, and consequently can command them to come out of human beings.

12.20.0.en: Since Satan is not good nor a follower of Christ, and does not gather people to believe in Him, this is a proof that he is an enemy of Christ, trying to scatter people and turn them away from Him, and he enters into people to lead them astray and make them lose their mind and insight. And Christ, by the authority of His divinity, drives His enemies the demons away from weak human beings, for He came to save mankind from the authority of the devil, who controls them because of their weakness and their sins. And by the Pharisees' accusing Him, they try to scatter people and turn them away from Him, and by this they are followers of the demons and enemies of Christ. He presents by this the fourth logical argument that He is against the demons and not with them, to rebuke the Pharisees so that they repent of their enmity toward Him, because, by their wickedness, they become followers of the demons who try to turn human beings away from God. Examine your words and your conduct: do they help draw others to God, or do they make them stumble and turn them away from Him, so that you may know whether you are a follower of Christ or of Satan?

12.21.0.en: Christ showed the gravity of the Pharisees' accusation against Him, which is that He casts out demons by an agreement with Satan, and not by the Holy Spirit.

12.21.1.en: Their insistence on rejecting the work of the Holy Spirit, and on not believing in Christ, will not be forgiven them forever, that is, it takes them to eternal torment. So He warns them to repent and not to persist in their evil thoughts. Whoever sins by a word against Christ the Son and repents, it is forgiven him, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit, and rejects His work in his life by insisting on not repenting, his fate is eternal perdition.

12.22.0.en: Christ rebukes the hypocrisy of the Pharisees, who pretend to be religious while their hearts are full of evil and pride, so He tells them that the good tree bears good fruit, and likewise the bad one bears bad fruit, and He requires them to keep away from hypocrisy, so that their words and works agree with the feelings of their hearts, and their thoughts are purified, that is, the inside becomes pure and likewise the outside, and if there is evil in the heart, it appears in speech or deeds, and that helps them to repent and reject sin.

12.22.1.en: The works of Christ, full of goodness and mercy, are good works that prove His righteousness and goodness, but the Pharisees, whose evil speech about Christ and whose pride prove that they are wicked; their bad fruits declare the evil of their hearts. And He rebukes them that this hypocrisy of theirs is like snakes in their cunning and outward smoothness, but they are full of poison and savagery and preying on others.

12.22.2.en: And by this He calls them to purify their hearts from the evils they have stored up inside them, which appear in their speech and their accusations.

12.23.0.en: "Idle word": that is, unprofitable, and what is meant here, most of all, is the evil speech by which we wrong others.

12.23.1.en: Christ shows the gravity of vain speech, that is, evil or unprofitable, since we will be held accountable for it on the day of judgment, so let us not take it lightly and speak words that are unprofitable or harmful to others. Our good speech justifies us on the day of judgment, and on the contrary, our evil speech, which shows that our hearts are evil, will lead us to perdition.

12.23.2.en: Examine your speech today: is it profitable to you or to others, or does it harm you or them, or is it of no use? And ask the help of God, and He will give you wisdom by His Holy Spirit.

12.24.0.en: "Master": the scribes and Pharisees said it, either in mockery or in flattery of Christ, that He might perform a new miracle for them.

12.24.1.en: Despite the many miracles of Christ, the scribes and Pharisees were still unbelieving, so they asked Him for a miracle that they might believe in Him, and this means that they were sunk in the doubts that obstruct faith.

12.25.0.en: "Generation": He means the Jewish nation, most of which is far from God by their evils, despite their appearing to be His people.

12.25.1.en: "Adulterous": the Jewish nation is the bride of God, and its departure from Him is spiritual adultery, for debauchery is a kind of adultery.

12.25.2.en: "Three days": a part of a day is counted as a day among the Jews, so in the death of Christ there was part of Friday, and the whole of Saturday, and part of Sunday.

12.25.3.en: "Three nights": what is meant is the darkness that occurred at His death on the Cross, and the night of Saturday and the night of Sunday.

12.25.4.en: "The heart of the earth": the tomb of Christ.

12.25.5.en: Christ rebuked the evils of their hearts and their persistence in pride and doubts, and told them that they did not need to see a new miracle of His miracles, but needed repentance, like the miracle of the repentance of Jonah the prophet, who repented in the belly of the whale after remaining in it three days, and died to the world, and returned to God, and then the whale spewed him out, and he returned alive. Just as Christ will die for the sins of the whole world, but by the power of His divinity will rise from the dead. They need to die to their sins by repentance, that they may believe in Him and rise from their evil, and begin the new life with Him.

12.26.0.en: "Nineveh": the capital of the Assyrian Empire, a city on the Tigris River in Iraq, near the present city of Mosul, and it was very great, its circumference 48 miles, and the height of its walls 28 meters, and it was destroyed in the sixth century before Christ.

12.26.1.en: When Jonah cried out powerfully among the people of Nineveh, after he had repented, his words had an effect on them and they repented. And now, before the Jews are words stronger than the words of Jonah, and great miracles, yet they refuse to believe. Therefore the repentance of the people of Nineveh will condemn the unbelief of those who reject Christ on the great day of judgment.

12.27.0.en: "The uttermost parts of the earth": that is, from a distance of about 1,000 miles from Jerusalem.

12.27.1.en: If the queen of the South and of Sheba, that is, Yemen, came from a distant place, when she heard of the wisdom of Solomon, and believed in the power of the Spirit of God in him, her faith also condemns the Jews who reject Christ, with His word and His perfect wisdom displayed before them.

12.28.0.en: "Dry places": Satan tends to dwell in the wastelands, where there is no water.

12.28.1.en: "Seeking rest": that is, seeking to do evil, because his rest is in turning people away from God.

12.28.2.en: When a demon entered a man, and by the power of God came out of him, he goes about seeking another person to dwell in. And since he finds no life for him for the good of people, he returns to see his old friend in whom he dwelt for a time, and finds his heart empty of all goodness, swept of all righteousness, indeed prepared and adorned with the evil in which he lives. For although he was delivered from Satan, he did not repent of his sins and live with God in goodness.

12.29.0.en: When he finds this man more prepared for his dwelling than before, he takes with him seven spirits (demons) and they dwell in him, to lead him into more evils, so his misery increases, and his end is perdition. So too the Jews, during the captivity they were bound to the worship of idols, and after their return they left it, but they were not bound to God in their hearts, and their hearts remained empty. And when Christ came to them and preached to them they rejected Him, and added to their sins the sins of hypocrisy and pride, so by this they prepare themselves for the work of the demons in them more than before, and their perdition becomes harder and their torment more severe.

12.29.1.en: When God delivers you from a sin, or removes its warfare from you and you rest a little from it, hasten to be bound to the Church and the Holy Sacraments, and keep on praying and reading, until your heart is filled with the love of God, and you become fortified against any new warfare from Satan.

12.30.0.en: While Christ was teaching among the crowds, His mother the Virgin Mary came, and the children of her sister Mary the wife of Cleophas, that is, the cousins of Christ on His mother's side.

12.30.1.en: In Jewish custom, cousins are counted as brothers. They came looking for Him, to enjoy sitting with Him and speaking to Him. And because of the great crowd around Him, they could not enter, so they told Him that outside the house were His mother and His brethren seeking Him.

12.31.0.en: Christ seized this opportunity to teach the crowds the meaning of spiritual motherhood and brotherhood, and He did not deny the importance of bodily motherhood and brotherhood, but wanted to direct the gaze of the crowds to a new meaning, which is that a person should have many mothers and brothers in the Spirit.

12.32.0.en: Christ showed that spiritual motherhood and brotherhood to Him are in whoever keeps His commandments and does His will; and the example of this is His disciples who follow Him.

12.32.1.en: For motherhood means self-giving and sacrifice, and brotherhood means fellowship and bonding. So whoever does the will of God must give up his personal desires, and strive to be bound to God and to the whole world in His love, and so he has spiritual motherhood and brotherhood toward God, and toward his brethren in the Church and the whole world.

12.32.2.en: Christ's esteem for you, and His calling you a brother, is a great honor that gives you boldness in prayer, and confidence in His help however much you fall into sin, that you may repent and return to Him.

12.32.3.en: And on the other hand, you keep yourself pure because you are a brother of Christ spiritually, and likewise you feel that all the believers with you in the Church are your brethren, so you love them and honor them with all care.

12.32.4.en: Thirteen. The parables of Christ; the preaching in His homeland
